title: Light & Shadows
description: Grade 4 Science: light and shadows — sources of light, how we see, how shadows form, transparent/translucent/opaque, and reflection in mirrors. Label the shadow and play.

topics.title: Sources of Light
topics.concept:
A source of light is anything that gives out its own light.

  • ☀️ Natural light sources: the Sun, stars, fireflies, lightning.
  • 💡 Man-made light sources: a bulb, a candle, a torch, a lamp.

Some things only LOOK bright but do not make their own light — like the Moon and a mirror. They simply bounce back light that falls on them.

recap: A light source gives out its own light.
Natural: Sun, stars, fireflies. Man-made: bulb, candle, torch.
The Moon and mirrors do not make light — they reflect it.

wonder.text: The Sun, a bulb and a candle all glow. But does the Moon make its own light?

qa.q: Does the Moon make its own light?
qa.a: No! The Moon does not make light. It shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces back to us. So the Moon's glow is really the Sun's light reflected.

qa.q: Is the Sun the most important light source?
qa.a: Yes — the Sun is our greatest natural light source. It lights up the whole day and helps plants make food. Without it, Earth would be dark and cold.

topics.title: How We See Things
topics.concept:
We can only see things when light reaches our eyes. Here is how seeing works:

  • 💡 Light from a source (like the Sun or a bulb) falls on an object.
  • ↩️ The object bounces some of that light back.
  • 👁️ The bounced light enters our eyes — and we see the object!

That is why we cannot see anything in total darkness — there is no light to bounce into our eyes.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="150" fill="#fff"/><text x="40" y="70" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">💡</text><defs><marker id="l1" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#FFC93C"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#FFC93C" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#l1)"><line x1="62" y1="64" x2="130" y2="70"/></g><text x="160" y="78" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🍎</text><defs><marker id="l1b" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#3CA7FF"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#3CA7FF" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#l1b)"><line x1="192" y1="70" x2="260" y2="64"/></g><text x="285" y="70" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle">👁️</text><text x="160" y="130" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Light bounces off into our eyes</text></svg>
recap: We see when light bounces off objects into our eyes.
Light travels from a source → object → our eyes.
In total darkness there is no light to see by.

wonder.text: In a completely dark room you see nothing at all. Why do we need light to see?

qa.q: Why can't we see in a dark room?
qa.a: Seeing needs light to bounce off objects into our eyes. In total darkness there is no light to bounce, so nothing reaches our eyes and we see nothing.

qa.q: Do cats see in the dark?
qa.a: Cats see much better than us in dim light because their eyes catch even tiny amounts of light. But in total darkness, even a cat cannot see!

topics.title: Shadows
topics.concept:
A shadow is a dark shape that forms when an object blocks light. Three things are needed to make a shadow:

  • 💡 A light source (the Sun or a torch).
  • 🧍 An object to block the light.
  • 🧱 A surface (the ground or a wall) for the shadow to fall on.

Shadows change size — they grow longer when the light is low (like evening Sun) and shorter when the light is high (like midday Sun).

recap: A shadow forms when an object blocks light.
You need a light source, an object and a surface.
Shadows are long when light is low, short when light is high.

wonder.text: Stand in the sunshine and a dark shape copies your every move on the ground. How is a shadow made?

qa.q: Why is my shadow long in the evening?
qa.a: In the evening the Sun is low in the sky. Low light hits you from the side and stretches your shadow out long. At midday the Sun is high, so your shadow is short.

qa.q: Can you have a shadow without light?
qa.a: No! A shadow needs a light source to be blocked. In the dark there is no light, so there are no shadows at all.

topics.title: Transparent, Translucent and Opaque
topics.concept:
Materials let light through in different amounts:

  • 🪟 Transparent — light passes through fully; you can see clearly (clear glass, clean water, air).
  • 🌫️ Translucent — only some light passes; you see blurrily (frosted glass, butter paper, thin curtain).
  • 🚪 Opaque — no light passes; you cannot see through (wood, brick, metal, your body).

Only opaque objects make clear, dark shadows, because they block all the light.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#f7f9ff"/><rect x="20" y="30" width="80" height="70" rx="6" fill="#cfeeff" stroke="#5aa0e0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="60" y="124" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Transparent</text><rect x="125" y="30" width="80" height="70" rx="6" fill="#dfe6ee" stroke="#9aa6b5" stroke-width="2"/><text x="165" y="124" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#6a7585" text-anchor="middle">Translucent</text><rect x="230" y="30" width="80" height="70" rx="6" fill="#a4724a" stroke="#7a5430" stroke-width="2"/><text x="270" y="124" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#7a5430" text-anchor="middle">Opaque</text></svg>
recap: Opaque: no light passes (wood) — these make dark shadows.

wonder.text: You can see clearly through a glass window, dimly through frosted glass, and not at all through a wooden door. Why the difference?

qa.q: Why does only an opaque object make a dark shadow?
qa.a: An opaque object blocks ALL the light, so the area behind it gets no light — making a clear, dark shadow. Transparent things let light through, so they barely make a shadow.
Clean water is transparent — you can see right through it. But muddy water is not, because the mud blocks the light. So it depends on what is in the water!

topics.title: Reflection and Mirrors
topics.concept:
Reflection is when light bounces off a surface. A smooth, shiny surface like a mirror reflects light so well that we see a clear picture, called an image.

  • 🪞 Mirrors and still water give clear reflections.
  • ↔️ In a flat mirror, your image is the same size but flipped left-to-right.
  • 🚗 Drivers use mirrors to see behind them.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#f0f6ff"/><text x="75" y="82" font-size="42" text-anchor="middle">🌷</text><rect x="146" y="18" width="9" height="114" rx="3" fill="#cfe0f0" stroke="#9fc4e0" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="24" x2="150" y2="60" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="3" opacity="0.7"/><g opacity="0.85"><text x="226" y="82" font-size="42" text-anchor="middle">🌷</text></g><text x="150" y="142" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">A mirror makes a reflection</text></svg>
recap: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface.
Smooth, shiny surfaces (mirrors) give a clear image.
A flat mirror flips your image left-to-right.

wonder.text: Look in a mirror and a copy of you looks back. How does a mirror bounce light so perfectly?

qa.q: Why does my reflection look flipped?
qa.a: A flat mirror swaps left and right. So when you raise your right hand, your mirror image seems to raise its left. Try it — wave and watch!

qa.q: Why can't I see myself in a wall?
qa.a: A wall is rough and dull, so it scatters light in all directions instead of bouncing it back neatly. Only smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors give a clear image.

questions.q: Which is a natural source of light?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a natural source of light; bulbs and torches are man-made.

questions.q: We can see an object when light…
options: Bounces off it into our eyes
questions.explanation: We see when light bounces off objects into our eyes.

questions.q: To make a shadow you need a light, a surface and…
options: An object to block the light
questions.explanation: A shadow needs an object to block the light.

questions.q: You can see clearly through a…
questions.explanation: Transparent glass lets light pass through, so you see clearly.

questions.q: A mirror gives a clear image because it…
options: Reflects light from a smooth surface
questions.explanation: A smooth, shiny mirror reflects light to give a clear image.
The Moon reflects the Sun's light; it makes none of its own.

questions.q: Why is your shadow longer in the evening than at midday?
options: The Sun is low in the sky and stretches it
questions.explanation: A low evening Sun hits you from the side and stretches your shadow long.

questions.q: Why can't you see yourself in a rough wall?
options: It scatters light instead of reflecting it neatly
questions.explanation: A rough wall scatters light, so it cannot form a clear image like a mirror.
Frosted glass lets only some light through — it is translucent.

questions.q: Moving a torch CLOSER to an object makes its shadow…
questions.explanation: A closer light makes a bigger shadow; a farther light makes it smaller.

questions.q: In a flat mirror, your image is…
options: The same size but flipped left-to-right
questions.explanation: A flat mirror gives a same-size image flipped left-to-right.
